claim: When the one answer-bearing passage is moved through a set of 10-30 retrieved passages, multi-document QA accuracy follows a U-shaped curve: highest when the passage comes first (primacy) or last (recency), and lowest in the middle. For GPT-3.5-Turbo the mid-context accuracy falls below its closed-book (no-document) accuracy of 56.1%.

experiment.location_in_paper: Section 2 (multi-document QA; Fig. 5, Table 1, Appendix G Tables 5-7), Section 3 (key-value retrieval; Fig. 7), Appendix E (Llama-2 sizes), Appendix F (GPT-4 on 500 examples)
experiment.task_or_benchmark: Multi-document QA over 2655 NaturalQuestions-Open queries whose annotated long answer is a paragraph. Each input has 1 gold Wikipedia passage plus k-1 distractor passages (k = 10, 20, 30) retrieved by Contriever (MS-MARCO fine-tuned) that do not contain the answer. There is also a synthetic JSON key-value retrieval task with 75, 140, or 300 UUID pairs.
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: The gold document's position is varied (e.g. index 0, 4, 9, 14, 19 of 20) while the order of the other documents is kept fixed. Prompt: 'Write a high-quality answer for the given question using only the provided search results (some of which might be irrelevant).' Greedy decoding. Ablations cover query-aware contextualization, randomly ordered distractors, and base vs instruction-tuned models.
experiment.evaluation_procedure: An answer counts as correct if any NaturalQuestions gold answer string appears in the model output. Closed-book and oracle (gold document only) baselines are reported.
experiment.main_comparison: Accuracy with the gold document at the start, middle, and end of the context, compared with the closed-book baseline
experiment.main_result: 20 docs, GPT-3.5-Turbo: 75.8% at index 0, 53.8% at index 9, 63.2% at index 19; closed-book 56.1%, oracle 88.3%. Claude-1.3: 59.9% / 56.8% / 60.1%. MPT-30B-Instruct: 53.7% / 52.2% / 56.3%. The U-shape also appears for GPT-4 and for Llama-2 13B/70B; Llama-2 7B shows only a recency bias. Extended-context versions (16K, 100K) perform almost identically to their base counterparts.

downstream.title: Positional Biases Shift as Inputs Approach Context Window Limits
downstream.summary: Read Sec. 1 and 4. Measures input length relative to each model's context window (Llama-3.x, Qwen2.5, Mistral-Small-3 and others). The Lost-in-the-Middle effect is strongest when inputs fill 50% of the window or less. Beyond that, primacy bias fades and a recency/distance bias remains, so the U-shape disappears. The authors note that 100K-token studies (e.g. InfiniteBench) did not find LiM.

downstream.title: Found in the Middle: Calibrating Positional Attention Bias Improves Long Context Utilization
downstream.summary: Section 2 (title 'Positional attention bias overpowers mid-sequence context') reproduces the U-shaped bias and attributes it to positional attention bias; calibrating that bias improves mid-context use. Only the search snippet and section headings were read.

downstream.title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching
downstream.summary: Read Sec. 4.4. Finds a lost-in-the-middle dip at 32K for 2024-25 models on one-hop NoLiMa questions. For two-hop questions, context length matters more than needle position.

downstream.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
downstream.summary: Appendix F.3 reports an analogous 'loss-of-middle-turns' effect: models over-weight the first and last conversation turns.

downstream_summary: The U-shaped position effect has been reproduced many times at the short input lengths of the original study (under ~6K tokens), including with 2024-25 open models. Later work shows it depends on how full the context window is: near the window limit, primacy fades and only recency or distance-to-end bias remains. Newer frontier models may show much smaller position effects on easy multi-document QA. Re-testing on modern models is informative and cheap.
notability_notes: One of the most cited LLM behavior papers. It coined the 'lost in the middle' phrase and underlies RAG reranking practice and many long-context benchmarks.
